other.label: CBO cost estimate: H.R. 4624, Muhammad Ali American Boxing Revival Act of 2026

summary: The Muhammad Ali American Boxing Revival Act of 2026 amends the Professional Boxing Safety Act of 1996 to establish private-sector Unified Boxing Organizations (UBOs) as an alternative regulatory framework for professional boxing. It introduces expanded medical, safety, anti-doping, and insurance requirements, sets a minimum pay standard per round, limits championship titles to one per weight class, and imposes conflict-of-interest prohibitions.

affected_groups.effect: Receive standardized minimum pay ($200 per round), mandatory health insurance coverage for match injuries and fatalities, expanded medical examinations, access to anti-doping programs, and alternative options via UBO contracts.
Must comply with new structural, medical, insurance, anti-doping, and financial transparency requirements, and face criminal penalties for willful violations.
Must establish procedures to ensure random and title-match drug testing and ensure matches occur only under regulated jurisdictions.
affected_groups.group: State Boxing Commissions and Tribal Organizations

affected_groups.effect: Must be certified and approved by either the state boxing commission or the Association of Boxing Commissions to participate in matches.

key_provisions: Authorizes the creation of private-sector Unified Boxing Organizations (UBOs) that operate alongside existing organizations and provide an alternative compliance system for boxers under contract.

Requires professional boxing matches to meet updated minimum medical standards, including specific time-valid physical examinations, eye checks, heart exams, antibody tests, and brain health assessments.
Mandates specific health insurance coverage of at least $50,000 for match injuries and $15,000 for accidental death, with premiums paid by promoters or UBOs rather than boxers.
Establishes a minimum payment requirement of $200 per round for all professional boxers participating in a match.
Limits sanctioning and unified boxing organizations to awarding only one championship title per weight class, and restricts the use of interim titles.
Requires state boxing commissions to ensure drug tests are administered for all title matches and at random for other matches.
Prohibits UBO officers or employees from holding financial interests in the management of boxers under contract or charging ranking and participation fees.
missing_information: Specific criminal penalties for promoters or entities other than UBO officers/employees who violate the act.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Muhammad Ali American Boxing Revival Act of 2026 amends the Professional Boxing Safety Act of 1996 to establish private-sector Unified Boxing Organizations (UBOs) as an alternative regulatory framework for professional boxing. It introduces expanded medical, safety, anti-doping, and insurance requirements, sets a minimum pay standard per round, limits championship titles to one per weight class, and imposes conflict-of-interest prohibitions.
summary_detail.significance: The bill updates federal regulation of professional boxing by introducing Unified Boxing Organizations, standardizing nationwide medical exams and anti-doping programs, establishing minimum pay and insurance floors for athletes, and altering rules for championship titles. Based on the rubric, this legislation has a moderate to substantial impact on the professional boxing industry, athletes, and regulatory commissions.
